0.content:
Varka met Barbatos as a reckless young knight who went to the Thousand Winds Temple and fought its Ruin Guard; the commotion woke the Archon, and the two became friends. He got his Vision thrilled that the Anemo Archon had noticed him, then got to know Barbatos and realised "that wasn't what it meant at all". He knows Venti is the Archon and keeps the secret. He calls him carefree but serious when it counts, with good taste in drink, and owes him drinks.

Barbatos mediated the Tripartite Conference with the Hexenzirkel, and Alice joked that Varka spoke so well Barbatos must have been feeding him lines. In 5.6, when Venti tried to call Alice, the call reached Varka mid-fight; he assumed it was about the drinks he owed and started telling him where his stash was before being cut off. From Nod-Krai he sent Venti a letter via Lohen, left at the Thousand Winds Temple since the Archon has no address.

Barbatos explained how to separate oneself from Lupus Boreas so as not to merge with the Ley Lines: "Focus on a single thought within the thousand winds". Varka admits he still does not understand it. In the 6.4 Homeward event (limited) they sat on the Anemo Archon Statue; Varka served grape juice because Charles would never forgive him for drinking without him, and when Venti asked whether a remark about Gnoses was a dig at him, Varka said he was not one to rub salt in old wounds.

1.content:
Jean credits Varka's teaching, along with her upbringing, for her devotion to duty, even though he takes duties lightly; what he leaves undone falls on her. He left her as Acting Grand Master when the expedition departed and told her that if he did not return, she would become Grand Master and train the next Knight of Boreas. He says she has the talent to be a far better Grand Master than he is, and she always says she is not qualified.

Drafting his letter to her after Nod-Krai, he grumbled that it was high time to drop the "Acting". His letter's postscripts asked her to find more honours for the Traveler and to be extra nice to Klee, offering to serve any solitary confinement for her himself. He swears he is not trying to dump his work on her; asked to swear on a glass of wine, he hesitates.

2.comment: Varka: Boreas and the Knight of Boreas
2.content:
The Knight of Boreas is the bridge between Mondstadt's people and Lupus Boreas, the Wolf of the North among the Four Winds. Only a few holders in a millennium won the wolf lord's real recognition, among them Ravenwood, Rostam and Varka. Varka earned it the hard way: he spent days fighting Boreas in Wolvendom, first thrashed, then trading blows, to relearn a lost sword style.

Boreas is half of Andrius, a wolf god from Nod-Krai who split his soul; the other half stayed in the north. Few Knights know this. Before the expedition Boreas warned Varka that a god's soul is a lethal poison to a human; Varka replied that only the Knight of Boreas can truly "answer" the God of the North Wind, and that his power is every person at his back. Boreas noted the brash young challenger had changed.

Varka jokes that the "Four Winds" make no sense, since "Wolf of the North" can mean Boreas or him and the Knights hold both the Lionfang and Boreas titles. The Knight of Boreas has a traditional homecoming song, first hummed by the Wandering Knight; on Varka's first expedition as Grand Master the Knights sang ancient songs on the training grounds for victory and a safe return.

3.content:
About half a year before the Traveler's arrival, Varka led the Knights' elite north with about eighty percent of their manpower, leaving Jean in charge. He went with little intelligence because he knew the Abyss was brewing in the north and could threaten all of Teyvat. The force included Seamus Pegg, Mika and Lohen. It did not expect to end up in Nod-Krai.

The expedition's secret task was to check on Andrius by following the trail Boreas took after the Wandering Knight, collecting wolf spirits broken off from the god. It crossed Snezhnaya, met Capitano, and reached Nod-Krai, where it worked out of The Flagship with the Northern Intelligence Network. Standing order: one knight, picked at random, stays sober whenever the others drink.

Letters home marked its progress: one via Mika at Weinlesefest (3.1, limited event) reporting the meeting with Capitano and asking Lisa to give Razor his parents' box; an open letter about Rerir; a cryptex letter to the Traveler carried by Ineffa (5.8); a letter to Jean after Dottore's defeat; and ten letters with Lohen (6.4). In camp the knights played a home-made tabletop war game with Varka as "Game Master".

4.content:
Lohen is the battle-loving Vice Captain of the Knights' 5th Company. Varka first thought he was a younger version of himself; he learned Lohen cares only for fighting, not glory, and when bored digs traps to ambush his Grand Master. Varka approved his promotion and took him on the expedition after Lohen asked how the Knights could protect Mondstadt if they could not protect themselves.

After Nod-Krai, Varka sent Lohen home with ten letters, the trigger for Varka's story quest. Lohen once spiked a gift of wine heavily enough to fell "twelve Forest Boars"; Varka shook it off.

In Lohen's story quest (6.6) Varka confronted him about a monster bearing Ursa the Drake's mark. Lohen swore an oath, the first Varka had ever heard from him, to finish things in a day, then vanished with Adorno. With the Traveler and Diluc, Varka tracked down the hidden laboratory where Theodore had restarted Eroch's experiments with Ursa's flesh, destroyed the remains and told Lohen to stay with Adorno to the end; punishments would come later.

5.content:
Varka met Razor in the forests of Wolvendom when the boy was barely taller than the wolf pups. He gave him the name Razor and taught him to use a claymore; learning to talk with him took half a year. Razor remembers him as a big man with a "big steelclaw" and wants to see him again.

Varka seems to have known Razor's parents and kept their mementos in a box in his office. During the expedition he wrote that it was time Razor learned about them (3.1, limited event). In barrel drills Razor spent three-quarters of a day trying to understand Varka's instructions.

6.content:
Eroch was an old friend who always told young Varka where he fell short of the chivalric code. Varka never saw that jealousy had taken root in him. On a later expedition Varka left Mondstadt with the veteran knights and Inspector Eroch; Dottore's Segments fed Eroch's resentment, and he roused an ancient horror that had been sealed, betraying every principle he guarded. Crepus died in that period. Varka returned in haste and rooted out the collaborators; cornered, Eroch took his own life laughing, a laugh Varka heard as mockery: you are only human after all.

Kaeya helped expose Eroch; Jean purged his traitors. Varka later wrote to Diluc apologising for Eroch. In 6.6 he recognised Eroch's old experiments on Ursa the Drake in Theodore's laboratory.

7.content:
Under the Anemo Archon's mediation, Varka sat at the Tripartite Conference and, with charm and talk, won a pact: the Hexenzirkel would help Mondstadt in its hour of need. He still calls a chat without drinks a "conference". Under the pact the mages built a trial; Varka fought it alone with joy and, asked to name a wish, only asked to glance into Barbeloth's scryglass.

It showed him glory, his childhood legends fighting real dragons, and a dark calamity in Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya with strangers wailing. He chose the north. He later wonders whether fate foresaw that he would try to change it. In 6.3 he invoked the pact to have Nicole help pull down the moon, spending the Hexenzirkel's last favour; hence his request that everyone be nice to Klee.

8.content:
In Nod-Krai Varka sent Ineffa to invite the Traveler to The Flagship but was away at Amsvartnir when they arrived. His squad ambushed the revived Rerir and was overpowered. In 6.1 he rescued the Traveler, Lauma, Flins, Aino and Columbina from the Wild Hunt, revealed The Flagship as the Knights' base and an intelligence hub, and with Albedo and Durin planned the trap that defeated Rerir. When Dottore took the moon's power and Columbina vanished (6.2), he rallied the despairing group. In 6.3 he organised evacuations and, while the Traveler fought Dottore, helped pull the moon down with Arlecchino and Nicole.

He asked Nefer to view Rerir's past and called Rerir's story tragic but no excuse. He sent Durin to warn Mondstadt, offering to waive his gliding exam if he flew fast enough. In his letter to Jean he noted the Fatui alliance with the Knave and Marionette, "may she rest in peace", and that the future stays uncertain until the Tsaritsa's intentions are known.

9.content:
Valentine, former Grand Master and Lionfang Knight, rejected young Varka from the Knights. Varka knocked out the examiners, then ambushed Valentine and his attendants that night, not having read the postscript of the rejection letter. Over drinks Valentine told him the free wind should not be caged too soon: go abroad, find your own reason to be a knight, and come back. Years later, by a winter campfire, Varka met Seamus Pegg, who had no one left in Nod-Krai; Seamus told him the people he missed were his answer, and made Varka "take him to Mondstadt" to see the dandelion wine, and Frederica.

Seamus, Frederica and Valentine later signed a birthday gift: a new off-hand sword, left unnamed.

10.content: During the limited 6.4 Homeward event, Diluc said Varka did a lot for him: he did not stop him leaving the Knights or put up roadblocks. Varka wrote from Nod-Krai apologising for Eroch and asking him to rejoin; Diluc declined. Varka keeps asking but fears the Dawn Winery blacklist. Varka knew Crepus from youth and said in Nod-Krai that Dottore murdered him. He trusts Kaeya completely because Kaeya chose to stay and helped expose Eroch.

key: To Those Who Embark on the Expedition
11.comment: Varka: The Heart of the Wolf
11.content:
With Rerir gone, the Abyss made an imitation of Roland, the Bloodstained Knight, and fused it with the corrupted Nod-Krai half of Andrius to lead the Wild Hunt. Killing the god risked disaster, so Varka chose a riskier plan: let himself be "killed" by Roland so he could reach the wolf's heart and let Andrius choose for himself. He had stored the wolf spirits in his own heart, not his sword. Andrius chose to return to the Ley Lines.

The letters Lohen carried were anchors: the people who received them pulled him back. On the way out he passed the swords of Rostam, Ravenwood and the Wandering Knight, and left Rostam's undelivered letter beside Roland's sword so the copy would know Rostam and Arundolyn never forgot him. He woke at Windrise surrounded by friends. During the quest a mysterious voice (Vedrfolnir) addressed him as Knight of Boreas; Varka first thought its eye was Dainsleif's. His first wish on recovering was to go back to Nod-Krai, partly to avoid paperwork.

12.comment: Varka: Arundolyn's Blade Dance and Varka's Vision
12.content: Arundolyn, the Lion of Light, was a Vision-less knight who fought with a claymore in one hand and a longsword in the other. No later knight matched him, and the Knights' records noted the dance's ferocity, not its technique. Varka had the strength but not the finesse, so he took wine and two blades to Wolvendom and fought Boreas for days. Boreas asked why the heavens had not noticed him; Varka pulled his Anemo Vision from behind his waist. He had not used it because Arundolyn made the dance without one. When he finally crossed his swords, the Vision blazed and he vowed to surpass his predecessor.

13.content: The expedition met the First Harbinger in the far north; Varka's letter home (3.1, limited event) said he was not hostile, that some of his actions had helped them (though he owed them that much), and that he had been ordered to Natlan. Leifhelm judged Capitano the only person they met whose strength compared to Varka's. Varka later remarked that he met him only once and that the "Sentinel Knight" Thrain of Khaenri'ah took his destiny into his own hands. He took heart in 6.4 that even Capitano could not take Mavuika's Gnosis by force.

14.comment: Varka: Favonius Keep and the Sober Watch
14.content: After Dottore's defeat Varka kept a small garrison at Favonius Keep and agreed with Nefer to make it a Northern Intelligence Network station for Abyss intelligence. In a world quest (6.3) he personally rescued a shipment of Dawn Winery dandelion wine, forbade anyone to open it until everyone was back, then skipped the party: it was his night as the camp's sober guard, drinking apple cider. Next day he had the Traveler work out which of Winfried, Ekbert and Leifhelm drank most: twenty laps for the worst, strength drills for the others.

15.comment: Varka: Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind (6.4 event)
15.content: During a limited-time 6.4 event, Alice and Nicole built a memory bubble so returning knights could relive the Traveler's first days in Mondstadt. Varka arrived hungover from drinks with Charles, sneaked in early and fought in the simulation. When the Abyss corrupted the bubble into a version where Dvalin had to be killed, Varka reassured the group it was not the Dvalin they knew and dealt the final blow; Paimon kicked him on the way out. At the banquet he thanked the Traveler for saving Mondstadt and, via Natlan, blunting the Wild Hunt, and said honour is something a knight defines for himself.

16.content: Varka's views of his knights: Mika is his "mentor" because lost marches need a map. Eula arranged the troops' reception at Dornman Port so well he was delighted. He is impressed by Noelle's strength and wonders if she could inherit his two-sword style, once she has had more training. Klee's solitary-confinement escapes are, he jokes, his teaching; Klee's basic training was postponed until she is older after she brought bombs to it. Albedo has loosened up enough to mock Varka's painting. Amber is the Knights' public face. He tried to make Lisa Captain of the 8th Company. He brought Rosaria to Mondstadt to redeem herself and will not discuss her past.

17.content: Aino calls him Uncle Varka; he prepaid her balanced meals and learned she did not need his worry. He asked Ineffa to carry his letter and thinks her escape from captivity will be an epic in Mondstadt. He values Nefer's network and Jahoda's grit, and would poach Jahoda if he dared. Flins makes him wish all aristocrats were like him. He told Lauma she had nothing to apologise for.

18.content: Varka respects the Pyro Archon as a warrior, as human or god, and wonders if a Natlan-born Varka could have crossed blades with her; but then he could not protect Mondstadt. An official anecdote says he once went to Natlan to see her, ended in a drinking contest at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, lost, and forgot why he had come.

19.comment: Varka: The Tankard and the Secret Stash
19.content: The Knights gave him a giant tankard, like a hammerhead: Huffman had the idea, Charles designed it, Wagner forged it, and about ten colleagues paid for it. He says it "balances" drinking bouts against his subordinates. He guards a secret stash and worries constantly that someone has found it. His old hiding spots from the office were the Cathedral spires and the Knights' rooftop; he says only Seamus, Frederica, Lohen and Mika could find him.
